Package hadur2.core.policy

Class DistancePolicy

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.DistancePolicy
public final class DistancePolicy extends Object
The distance Hadur tries to fight at (the artifact's distance controller). 1.20 held a fixed 650 px, which on an 800x600 field is a retreat: bullets take 33-45 ticks to arrive and our own gun's escape angle is at its widest.
  • The target starts at the opening's distance (CEILING for a stranger, so a stranger meets 1.20's distance until this battle's evidence says otherwise).
  • DIST-1: on each enemy wave, while our rolling hit rate exceeds theirs by GAP or more, the target comes in STEP px, not below FLOOR (400 px; the artifact's 150 px cost score share, see the constant). While theirs exceeds ours by as much, it goes back out a step, not beyond CEILING.
  • DIAL-1: coming in is the aggressive setting, so the lead must be certain: the gap between the two estimates' centres, less its 95% margin (the two margins combined), must still be GAP or more. Going out is the conservative one and needs no certainty. (With only "a lead of any size is certain", the S5 bench saw a cold battle against Shadow, where the two rates are equal, walk in to 175 px on noise: 100-shot windows checked on every wave of 35 rounds find a false lead sooner or later.)
  • END-1: while finishing, the target is FINISH whatever the controller holds; the controller's own target is kept for when the endgame ends.

Where it sits in the tick: HadurCore makes one per opponent from the opening book's distance, calls onWave(hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate) once for each enemy wave that broke this tick, with the two HitWindow estimates, and hands target(boolean) to the surf as its desired distance. MOVE-2's last flavour moves the band out through shiftOut(double). The target is a centre-to-centre distance in px and always lies in [FLOOR, CEILING], apart from END-1's FINISH.

  • Field Details

    • FLOOR

      public static final double FLOOR
      The closest the controller goes. The artifact said 150; the S5 bench put it at 400: at 150 px the sample bots' head-on and linear guns hit Hadur often enough to cost a point or two of score share, and 300 still cost a little, while 400 kept every sample bot's share at its S4 level and still ended rounds sooner. END-1 still closes to 150 to finish, where the enemy is nearly dead and its gun is the hotter one.

  • Method Details

    • onWave

      public DistancePolicy.Step onWave(Estimate ours, Estimate theirs)
      DIST-1: one enemy wave's step, from both rolling hit rates.

      The 5-point test reads the raw rates, and the step in also needs certainLead(hadur2.core.memory.Estimate, hadur2.core.memory.Estimate) (DIAL-1). The step out needs only the raw gap, since further is the conservative side. An empty window (NaN rate) holds the target.

      Parameters:
      ours - our rolling hit rate on them
      theirs - their rolling hit rate on us
      Returns:
      which way the target moved

    • certainLead

      public static boolean certainLead(Estimate ours, Estimate theirs)
      DIAL-1: whether our rate leads theirs by at least GAP beyond the 95% margin of the difference.

      For two independent estimates the margin of their difference is the root of the sum of their squared margins (Math.hypot). The gap is taken between the Agresti-Coull centres (Estimate.center()), which the margins are measured from, so a window of 0 hits in 3 shots does not read as a certain 0%.

      Parameters:
      ours - our rolling hit rate on them
      theirs - their rolling hit rate on us
      Returns:
      whether the lead is at least GAP with 95% confidence
